title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer to prevent regional failover storms and excessive load-shedding
author: Priya Patel
commits: 3f9a1b2: add regional failover hysteresis and cooldown window to prevent repeated failovers
7b2d4c5: introduce queue ordering guard to reduce ordering-induced thrashing under high load
a1c4e7d: soften load-shedding thresholds for legacy clients, add gradual backoff policy
d5f8e9a: expose internal metrics for in-flight failover operations and shed counts
e2b3f1c: add unit and integration tests for hysteresis/backoff and update config defaults
f0a9d6b: add feature-flag to toggle strict shedding for canary rollout and CI gating
description:
Summary: Fixes a production issue where SLO enforcer state transitions could trigger rapid regional failovers and aggressive load-shedding during transient pressure. This caused client-facing errors and cascading throttles across regions. The hotfix adds hysteresis, cooldown windows, queue-ordering guards, and a safer default shedding profile to prevent repeated failovers and over-shedding.

Background and motivation: Over the past two weeks (ENG-8273) we observed multiple incidents where the enforcer considered ephemeral latency spikes as sustained violations. The enforcer would promote regional failover as a mitigation and concurrently increase load-shedding thresholds aggressively. Because failovers were processed without sufficient cooldown or ordering guarantees, this created a feedback loop: failing region ramps down, traffic moves to other regions, which then also failover -> system thrashes.

What this change does:
- Adds a configurable hysteresis window (default 30s) to regional failover decisions to require sustained SLO breach before triggering.
- Adds a cooldown window after a failover (default 2m) to prevent immediate re-evaluation and flapping.
- Introduces queue-ordering guard logic to prefer draining high-priority queues first and avoid interleaved rejections that lead to ordering races.
- Softens default load-shedding policy for legacy clients and adds gradual backoff (multi-step shed) instead of hard cutoffs.
- Emits new metrics (slo_enforcer.failover_inflight, slo_enforcer.shed_count_by_priority, slo_enforcer.hysteresis_trips) for observability and postmortem analysis.
- Feature-flagged strict shedding behavior so we can roll out the change to a small canary before enabling org-wide.
- Adds unit and integration tests, and an e2e hysteresis test to the CI.

Files touched (high level):
- region_failover_manager.rs: implement hysteresis + cooldown + metrics.
- queue_ordering.rs: ordering guard to avoid interleaved rejections during high pressure.
- load_shedding.rs: staged shedding policy and feature flag checks.
- configs/defaults/slo_enforcer.yaml: tune defaults to less aggressive shedding and enable hysteresis.
- observability config: add metric names and dashboard hints.
- docs/ops/slo-enforcer-runbook.md: update runbook to include new knobs and rollback steps.
- ci scripts: add integration test step for canary flag.

Testing and CI:
- Local unit tests for hysteresis and shedding added.
- Integration test simulates region latency spike and asserts single failover with cooldown.
- e2e test verifies staged shedding behavior across priority queues.
- CI initially failed (flaky test), fixed by increasing test timeouts; all checks passing on final push.

Review notes and risk assessment:
- Risk: changing failover hysteresis and shedding defaults affects runtime behavior under pressure. Mitigations: feature-flag default OFF for strict shedding; canary rollout to 10% traffic; metrics added for rapid detection.
- Risk: ordering guard could increase tail latency for some low-priority requests; mitigations: staged shedding profile and per-queue thresholds.

Related: ENG-8273 (incident), ENG-8290 (postmortem + followups), SUP-1182 (support cases from legacy clients).

Checklist: [x] add tests [x] update configs [x] document runbook [x] add metrics [x] feature-flag enabled [x] CI green

Commit summary: see commits list.

Review conversation (high level):
- Maya Singh: requested adding cooldown window and suggested metric names; I updated region_failover_manager and added metrics.
- Ethan Park: asked for clearer defaults in slo_enforcer.yaml and an admin knob to disable strict shedding; added admin flag and docs.
- Luca Bianchi: verified unit tests and suggested an integration test for cross-region traffic surge; added e2e test.
- Priya (author): replied to all comments, iterated on tests and added CI gating for canary.

CI summary: First CI run had one flaky integration test failing under constrained runner (timeout). Increased timeout and re-ran, all checks passed: unit tests, integration tests, lint, build, and canary deployment simulation. ci/slo-enforcer-checks.yml added to CI pipeline.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main. Post-merge, canary rolled out to 10% and monitored for 6h; no increased error rates observed and shedding counts decreased in targeted scenarios. Full rollout scheduled via feature-flag toggle after 24h of monitored stability.

Release notes: Hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer to avoid regional failover storms and excessive load-shedding; adds hysteresis & cooldown, queue-ordering guards, safer shedding defaults, new metrics, and feature-flagged rollout.
